doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Being straight ahead as a person and not selling himself
summary: He says his unpretentious philosophy may have cost him promotion, but he is who he is.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well I just had my 15 minutes of glory with you again, and so like that’s, I don’t know how many altogether. I’m like in interview heaven.

That’s my philosophy. And believe me that philosophy has created me, maybe it hasn’t been that good for me because this is who I am. I don’t sell myself, I don’t know how to sell myself. Sometimes in this business you need to portray yourself as a very important person and keep distance, and that creates a mystery that people want to, oh, Ignacio, oh you know he’s an enigma. No I’m straight ahead. That’s the way I am, that’s the way I’m going to die, and that’s the way I like it, straight ahead jazz. And I’m straight ahead. You know that doesn’t mean that I’m going to allow nobody to disrespect me. I know who I am. But I’m straight ahead. I’m a human being. Hey, come on.
